title: Forbidden Now, Possible Later
notes: Open with the paradox, because it is the cleanest way to motivate the whole chapter. A car cannot move sideways at an instant, and a rolling contact cannot slip in its forbidden direction. Yet the driver can parallel park, and a rolling contact can reorient through sequences. Tell students that the lecture is about the mathematical object that reconciles those facts: a velocity distribution whose brackets may create effective directions not present at first order.

title: Pfaffian Constraints
notes: Spend time on the row interpretation. A matrix row is not just an algebraic object; it is a covector that tests a candidate velocity. The distribution Delta is what remains after all tests return zero. That distinction matters later, because integrability asks whether these allowed tangent planes fit together into configuration-space surfaces, while nonholonomy asks what motion sequences can do when they do not.

title: From One-Forms To Allowed Directions
notes: Use the image as a bridge between covectors and motion. The one-form is easier to compute with, but the distribution is easier to reason about geometrically. Ask the class to read a single point first: which drawn direction survives the Pfaffian test? Then zoom out and ask the integrability question: do these directions assemble into sheets, or do their brackets force motion out of any candidate sheet?

title: Holonomic, Partially Holonomic, Completely Nonholonomic
notes: The goal is to prevent students from treating nonholonomic as a synonym for difficult. Holonomic constraints have enough first integrals to define leaves. Partially holonomic systems sit between the extremes: brackets add directions, but not all directions. Completely nonholonomic systems are the dramatic case for planning, because the Lie closure reaches the full tangent space. Keep the terms tied to rank and leaves, not to intuition alone.

title: Vector Fields And Flows
notes: This slide sets up the bracket square by making flows concrete. A vector field is an assignment of tangent vectors, but a flow is the result of following that assignment for time t. In control language, each admissible input selects a vector field or combination of vector fields. The later bracket formula is not an abstract algebra trick; it is the leading error term produced when four short flow segments are composed in a loop.

title: Lie Bracket Flow Square
notes: Make the cancellation explicit. Four small moves appear to return the system to its starting point if students only add first-order arrows. The image and formula show why that reasoning is incomplete: the flows are evaluated at shifted points, so a second-order term survives. Connect this directly to parking and rolling examples. The forbidden direction is not violated instantaneously; it is accumulated through a loop of legal motions.

title: Bracket Algebra Rules
notes: Treat the rules as a computational grammar. Bilinearity lets students expand candidate fields, antisymmetry prevents double counting, Jacobi identifies dependencies among nested brackets, and the function-coefficient rule explains why brackets are not merely formal symbols with scalar labels. Emphasize that the algebra is used to build a rank test, so simplification is not cosmetic. It decides whether a proposed new direction is genuinely independent.

title: Frobenius: Leaves Versus Brackets
notes: This is the conceptual hinge of the lecture. Frobenius turns a geometric question about leaves into a bracket calculation. If all brackets of tangent vector fields remain inside the distribution, the allowed planes fit together as tangent planes to submanifolds. If a bracket points outside, then loops of allowed motion detect a direction that no leaf could contain. That is precisely the phenomenon students saw in the flow square.

title: Pfaffian Integrability Test
notes: Give students the chapter's actual test route. First ask whether a single Pfaffian equation has an integrating factor that turns it into an exact differential. For multiple one-forms, build the annihilating distribution Delta equals Omega perpendicular, then use Frobenius to test bracket closure. The point is not to introduce a new exterior-calculus toolbox; it is to show how the one-form view and the vector-field view meet.

title: Chow And The Rank Condition
notes: After Frobenius says when leaves exist, Chow says why the opposite case can be powerful. A bracket-generating distribution gives a reachability statement: even though controls are restricted to horizontal directions, enough short loops can synthesize the missing directions. Be careful with the practical caveat. The theorem guarantees connectivity under its hypotheses, but it does not hand over an efficient trajectory, account for actuator bounds, or solve obstacle avoidance.

title: Where Nonholonomy Comes From
notes: Use examples to anchor the formalism without replacing it. Rolling and steering give contact-level no-slip equations, while angular-momentum conservation gives velocity constraints even when there is no wheel on the ground. Hoppers and space robots are important because they show that nonholonomy is not only a rolling phenomenon. It can also appear when internal shape change is coupled to conserved momentum.

title: Kinematic Car
notes: Use the car to make Pfaffian notation feel physical. The form minus sine theta dx plus cosine theta dy measures sideways body-frame motion, and the constraint sets that measurement to zero. The car can drive forward and change orientation, but not translate sideways at an instant. The parking maneuver is therefore not a violation of the constraint; it is a sequence that changes orientation and accumulates a lateral net effect.

title: Rolling Disk And Fingertip
notes: The dashboard should be read as a rank story, not just as a plot. For a rolling disk, the no-slip rules are velocity constraints at the ground contact. For a rolling fingertip, the same logic is lifted into two moving surface frames. In both cases, first-order allowed directions may be too few, and the growth vector tells how quickly bracket operations add missing directions.

title: Filtration And Degree Of Nonholonomy
notes: Connect this definition back to computation. A rank condition is not checked by listing all possible brackets forever. The filtration organizes the search by depth. At each step, add brackets between original allowed directions and the directions already discovered. The degree of nonholonomy measures how many layers of this process are needed before the system sees the full tangent space.

title: Philip Hall Basis
notes: Present the Hall basis as an algorithmic convenience with mathematical depth. When there are several control fields, the number of formal nested brackets grows rapidly. Antisymmetry tells us some words only differ by sign, and Jacobi tells us some combinations are dependent. A Hall ordering supplies a disciplined list of representatives, which is why it appears naturally when implementing rank-growth checks.

title: Computational Check And Lab
notes: Close by connecting the abstract lecture to the executable artifacts. The final sanity payload verifies the intended bracket direction and the second-order scaling of the bracket loop. The lab then asks students to rerun the diagnostic under a small perturbation and explain the invariant, rather than merely reporting a plot. This is the habit the chapter is trying to build: every geometric claim should have a visible object and a compact computational check.
